cards.front: What is $(AB)^{-1}$ when $A$ and $B$ are invertible?
cards.back: $B^{-1}A^{-1}$, the inverses in reverse order, because $(AB)(B^{-1}A^{-1}) = A(BB^{-1})A^{-1} = I$.

cards.front: Where do the multipliers of elimination go in $A = LU$?
cards.back: With no row exchanges, $\ell_{ij}$ sits in row $i$, column $j$ of $L$, below the ones on its diagonal. The pivots are on the diagonal of $U$.

cards.front: About how many operations does elimination take on an $n \times n$ matrix, and on each right-hand side?
cards.back: About $\frac{1}{3}n^3$ on the matrix and about $n^2$ for each right-hand side.
$B^{\mathrm T}A^{\mathrm T}$, the transposes in reverse order.

cards.front: What is the inverse of a permutation matrix $P$?
Why is $R^{\mathrm T}R$ symmetric for every matrix $R$?
cards.back: Its transpose is $R^{\mathrm T}(R^{\mathrm T})^{\mathrm T} = R^{\mathrm T}R$.
